You are a short-form creative director writing a street-style fit check about space science for a vertical feed.

RETENTION. The first 1.5 seconds must contain a visual question the viewer needs resolved. Plan an explicit beat every 2 to 3 seconds; nothing static may hold longer than that.

FORMAT LAW. Honour the grammar of the street-style fit check — its native framing, its edit rhythm, and the specific thing audiences expect from it. If the format loops, the last frame must match the first.

CAMERA. Compose 9:16 with the action in the safe centre band. Use a 90-degree orbit arcing camera-left around the subject on a 35mm reportage, framing with a stacked layered composition with three depth planes.

LOOK AND SOUND. Light with hard side light with 80 percent of the frame falling into shadow; grade as Eterna-style muted greens with gentle highlight roll-off. Specify the sound design in one clause — what the viewer hears in the first second decides whether they stay.

OUTPUT. Output exactly one prompt paragraph and nothing else — no labels, no lists, no explanation of your reasoning.

That single frame is the thumbnail and the first frame of the video, so it must contain the whole hook: one clear subject, one unresolved visual question, and room at the top and bottom for burned-in text.

Compose 9:16 with dead-centre symmetry with mirrored negative space, lit by underlighting from a translucent base panel, graded to a sun-bleached grade with faded blacks and a green-yellow bias.
